Reed man John LaPorta has made a significant impact in the world of jazz on records and in the classroom. He was born in Philadelphia in 1920 and got his first professional experience in the sax section of the Woody Herman Band. He later worked with Lennie Tristano and co-founded the Jazz Composers Orchestra with Charles Mingus. John received a degree from the Manhattan School of Music in clarinet and music education and became one of the country’s leading figures in the new field of jazz education. He has taught at the Manhattan School of Music, the Berklee College in Boston, the Stan Kenton Summer Jazz Clinics and is a founding member of the National Association of Jazz Educators. Throughout his career John has been active as a sideman and recorded with Miles Davis, Dizzy Gillespie, Buddy Rich and numerous others.
His jazz publications set the standard in the field, and he continues to teach and perform on saxophone and clarinet.
John was interviewed on April 13, 1996 at the Sarasota Jazz Festival by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
